editorNote: Updated international examples and evidence sections with recent findings from key UBI experiments and policy analyses. Maintained neutral tone and cited only provided sources.

examples.summary: Finland conducted a basic income experiment providing unconditional monthly payments to unemployed individuals to assess effects on employment and well-being.
lessons: The experiment provided insights into the impact of basic income on recipients' employment incentives and psychological well-being, though detailed outcomes require further review.
sources: Kela - Results of Finland's basic income experiment

examples.summary: GiveDirectly launched the world’s largest and longest universal basic income study, distributing monthly cash transfers to individuals in extreme poverty across multiple villages.
lessons: Preliminary findings indicate that basic income improves food security, helps recipients manage shocks, and enables long-term planning and investment. Large one-time transfers may yield better economic outcomes than short-term monthly payments.

examples.summary: The Stockton Economic Empowerment Demonstration (SEED) provided $500 monthly unconditional cash payments to 125 randomly selected residents for 24 months.
lessons: Guaranteed income reduced income volatility, improved mental and physical health, and supported recipients in finding full-time employment. It also enhanced recipients' financial stability and agency.

examples.summary: The Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend distributes annual dividends to all residents from state oil revenues, providing a universal cash payment but not a full basic income.
lessons: The program demonstrates a sustainable model of universal cash distribution linked to natural resource revenues, though it differs from a full UBI in scope and amount.

analysis.title: Fiscal and Policy Considerations of Basic Income
analysis.summary: The OECD highlights the comparative framing of basic income policies and the fiscal trade-offs involved, emphasizing the need to balance social objectives with budgetary constraints.
sources: OECD - Basic Income as a Policy Option

analysis.title: Work Incentives and Universal Basic Income
analysis.summary: The IMF discusses how universal basic income schemes affect work incentives and the framing of such policies, noting potential impacts on labor market participation and economic behavior.
sources: IMF - Universal Basic Income and Work
